text: Through forest deep we walked as one. Yellow bricks beneath the sun. But shadows whispered through the trees and sudden roars would steal the breeze. I leapt into the road with pride, but fear was clawing deep inside. I struck the tin. I swiped at straw. Yet dread within was all I saw. >> Don't you dare to bite, my friend. >> I swear no harm was mine to send. You are nothing but a cowardly king. I

Know. And it is a painful thing.  The king of beasts or so they say, but I just roar and run away. Elephants, tigers, all take flight while I'm the one consumed by fright. He is so large yet small inside. A trembling heart he cannot hide. Oh lion bold, what sorrows there to wear a crown of cold despair. Brave you seem but fear you feel. A king in name with wounds to heal. Brave you seem, but fear you feel. A king in name with wounds to heal.

Perhaps my heart is weak and worn. A lion lost, ashamed for lawn. If Oz can gift me strength a new, then maybe I can stand with you. You'll walk with us. You'll find your grace. The bravest heart is not the face. Together now we'll seek the way and courage find with each new day. Then let me walk beside you all. Though trembling heart, I'll stand tall. And though I know my roar is a bluff, I'll brave this road, though rough and tough. The truest courage not to fight, but walk through fear into the light. And so we go through field and wood together now for greater good.
